title: Stability class routing matrix for version anchoring
content:
Purpose:

This is a working note capturing a proposed compatibility/behavior matrix and operational guidance for how model registry "version anchoring" (what folks commonly call pinning) should interact with routing policies across regions, capacity tiers, and fallback topologies. The goal is to make the control-plane semantics unambiguous for SREs, infra, and product teams and to capture trade-offs for latency, availability, and long-tail cost.

Status/context: draft exploratory — intended to complement the registry design doc and the routing policy spec. Not final; meant to capture edge cases that have tripped us up in staging.

Definitions / framing assumptions:
- Version anchoring: customer-level binding of a route to a specific model version (e.g., model-x:v3.2). Distinct from soft affinity where a route prefers a model but may accept compatible fallbacks.
- Stability class: a derived label per model-version computed by registry / review process (stable | beta | experimental) that informs routing tolerance to fallbacks and region routing.
- Routing tiers: {premium, standard, best-effort} used by control plane for cost/latency decisions.
- Compatible variant: any model variant that preserves API compatibility and required capabilities (e.g., tool-calling, streaming).
- Rollout window: time-limited canary or staged rollout period where anchors may be temporarily relaxed for safety.

High-level requirements we want to satisfy:
1) Anchored routes must observe customer-level SLA and not silently degrade quality by switching to incompatible variants.
2) System must provide graceful degradation strategies (fallback to older stable versions, region failover) without violating data isolation or pinned version semantics unless explicitly configured.
3) Control plane must be able to make routing decisions using signals: stability class, telemetry (error rate/latency), regional capacity, and explicit tenant policy (strict vs flexible anchoring).
4) Operators must have clear visibility (telemetry + decision provenance) for any automatic routing deviation from an anchor.

Proposed compatibility matrix (text table):
Columns: Anchor stability class | Request routing policy | Allowed fallback classes | Region failover allowed? | Require explicit consent to change | Control plane action notes

1) stable | strict | none | no | yes | Reject requests if anchored version unavailable; return 503 with pin-status header.
2) stable | prefer | stable | yes | no | Route to anchored version when available; if not available route to nearest stable variant in same tier/region and mark trace/span with fallback reason.
3) beta | prefer | stable,beta | yes | no | Prefer anchored beta; if cannot route and stable variant exists in same model family, allow fallback to stable.
4) beta | flexible | stable,beta,experimental | yes | no | Control plane may route to compatible experimental variant within same region when capacity constrained—log and emit alert if quality regressions detected.
5) experimental | flexible | experimental | no | no | Experimental anchors are treated as hints; routing can substitute any experimental-compatible variant. Operators get increased telemetry retention for these routes.
6) any | emergency-fallback | stable | yes | no | Emergency-fallback is an operator-initiated override (SRE/APIs) to ensure availability: route to most recent stable in a region with data isolation constraints respected.

Notes on semantics: the matrix distinguishes "strict" vs "prefer" vs "flexible" tenant settings. Tenant admin UI will expose an anchor policy toggle (Strict: fail on mismatch; Prefer: fallback allowed but notify; Flexible: heuristics apply).

Control plane decision flow (sketch):
1) Receive request with route and tenant anchor metadata.
2) Resolve anchored model version + stability class from registry.
3) Evaluate local region capacity and latency SLO candidate set for the anchored version.
4) Apply tenant routing policy + stability matrix to determine allowed fallback set.
5) If anchored version available and within SLO -> route.
6) If not available: (a) if strict -> fail with explicit pin-status; (b) else compute best compatible fallback by cost/latency rank and route with provenance header/trace and alert if crossing stability boundary.
7) Persist decision traces for audit and rollback visibility.

Multi-region considerations and data isolation:
- Customer data residency requirements must be enforced before any region fallback. Control plane should attach a per-tenant region-allowlist; fallbacks that cross disallowed regions must be blocked even if technically compatible.
- In multi-region capacity storms, prefer cross-region fallbacks only for tenants with explicit cross-region consent. Otherwise use best-effort local pool or fail based on strictness.
- For on-prem/private deployments, fallbacks to hosted variants must be disabled unless explicit hybrid policy configured.

Telemetry and operator UX:
- Emit pin-decision spans: anchored_version, actual_version_served, stability_classes, fallback_reason, control_plane_rule_id.
- Pin-status header returned to caller: pin-status:{ok|fallbacked|blocked}, pin-info:version+class.
- Alerting: set low-threshold regression alerts for routes with anchoring changes (e.g., sudden spike in hallucination or latency after fallback).
- Console: pinning audit timeline per route showing decisions, metrics, and the region/capacity reasons for any deviation.

Edge cases and examples:
- Example A: Tenant A pins to model-x:v8 (stable) in us-west; strict policy. us-west deck goes down. In strict mode, requests should fail with 503 and pin-status=blocked. Operators can manually invoke emergency-fallback to model-x:v7-stable in us-east with audit log.
- Example B: Tenant B pins to model-y:v3 (beta); policy prefer. Us-east saturated for v3; control plane chooses v3-beta in us-west (same family) if tenant allows cross-region; serves with pin-status=fallbacked and annotated quality check.
- Example C: Tenant C pinned to experimental variant with flexible policy. Control plane swaps to a quantized variant in same family to reduce cost/latency when load high — but because class is experimental, this is allowed. Post-change evals are run automatically to detect regressions.

Operational safeguards / rollout guidance:
- New anchoring semantics should be behind a feature flag per tenant for 6 weeks. Incrementally enable for a few enterprise customers and watch for breakage.
- Add preflight checks in the console when tenant attempts to anchor to a version that lacks compatible fallbacks (console warns about strict mode behavior).
- Provide a one-click emergency-fallback in the SRE console that records justification and requires 2 approvers for cross-region fallbacks for regulated tenants.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to encode compatibility at finer granularity (capability matrix e.g., tool-calling, streaming, embeddings) and have routing use capability-level constraints rather than coarse stability classes? (Ticket: JIRA-REG-901)
- Should we offer per-route "grace window" where an anchor can be auto-relaxed for X minutes during transient infra outages? If so, what signaling is safe?
- How do we tie model-quality regression alerts to automatic rollback decisions? Need a playbook for automated rollback vs operator intervention.

Next steps:
- Prototype control-plane decision simulator (small service) that can replay traffic and exercise matrix behaviors. Owner: Marco Li. (linked: github.com/redwood-inference/registry#42)
- Add schema changes to registry to persist stability_class and declared compatible capabilities per model-version. Owner: Evelyn Chen. (confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-2345)
- Draft console UX copy for anchor policy toggle and preflight warnings. Owner: Product-Console team.

Appendix — quick checklists for SREs:
- If tenant reports degraded quality after fallback: check pin-decision spans -> identify actual_version_served -> run comparison evals from stored prompt sets.
- If region outage: verify tenant region-allowlist before invoking emergency-fallback.
- Keep emergency-fallbacks logged and auto-escalated to compliance for regulated tenants.

Notes-to-self: keep matrix small and conservative. Prefer defaults that protect customer expectations (fail loud rather than silently degrade) and expose telemetry to make exceptions safe.

References: internal routing policy draft, model registry schema PR, SRE runbook on region failover (see linked_artifacts above).

-- A.P.
